title: Ancient Beauty Reborn
shortDescription: One-of-a-kind Urushi art that never shows the same expression twice. Master artisan Kodai Yamauchi breathes the spirit of Japan's oldes

owner.bio: Chuyên gia phát triển dự án bất động sản và nông nghiệp công nghệ cao.

content:
This isn't just a charm — it's a small act of forest
conservation you can hold in your hands. Thinning wood
is harvested to keep forests healthy, and instead of
being discarded, it's reborn as a beautiful keepsake
carrying the natural fragrance of Hinoki.

With 6 days remaining, let's make this happen together.
Share this project with someone who would love a piece
of Japanese craftsmanship.

Thank you for being part of this journey.

KODAI WORKS / Kodai Yamauchi 
![Image](https://i.kickstarter.com/assets/053/758/200/c30af13986ee70503472e29744d1d190_original.jpg?fit=scale-down&origin=ugc&q=92&v=1778989319&width=680&sig=II0WgIU7znWhloCP0K67vWKhCWvd7f4X1UeJoWwG1Pw%3D)
9,000 years ago, the world’s oldest Urushi (lacquer) culture was born in Japan. It was an ancient wisdom that viewed a single drop of sap as a "membrane of prayer," connecting humans with nature and the great flow of time. In today’s world of efficiency and speed, have we forgotten the quiet moments of reflection?

Urushi is not merely a traditional coating. It possesses a mysterious luster emerging from darkness and a tactile quality that feels as if it’s breathing. It is a living energy that hardens and clears over time, growing alongside its owner. Now, from the heart of Echizen, Fukui, a lacquer artist awakens these ancient memories. We invite you to welcome a "moment of Urushi"—an expression that will never be replicated—into your daily life.

title: Nagoya Folding Fans: Bring a cool breeze with ease in Summer
shortDescription: Crafted by skilled Japanese artisans using traditional fan-making techniques, cool down wherever you are with just a flick of the wrist

owner.bio: Chuyên gia phát triển dự án bất động sản và nông nghiệp công nghệ cao.

content:
![Image](https://i.kickstarter.com/assets/053/677/892/952ed1ed365043be0df711cd5c1967d8_original.png?fit=scale-down&origin=ugc&q=100&v=1778487037&width=680&sig=d8bRBmH75UQztVpG3pOOxvxoOql16pRPArSpTS36oiI%3D)
How we approach the summer heat has changed over time. Today is a time when we can use powerful cooling units to blast cold air, but in ancient Japan, there was a way of making wind just for you.

The sensu or folding fan is that tool. A small design made of bamboo and washi paper, with just a little bit of movement, creates cooling air and allows you to create just the right amount of cool air for you. Not reliant on electricity, and without disturbing things around you, you can quietly create a comfort for yourself. Used in traditional Japanese dance known as Nihon Buyo, as well as Noh, Japanese theatrical art, it is a tool that brings beauty to the movement of the fan itself.

With each waft of the fan, a cooling breeze will flow against the face and neck, and in just a few seconds, your body and feeling will cool down and settle. Just like a brief moment of meditation, this is an item that will offer a moment of reset.

Through this project, we hope to share a way of thinking that has endured in Japanese daily life, expressed through folding fans crafted by the hands of skilled artisans.

title: The Marvel Art of MIKE ZECK - A Deluxe Art Book and more!
shortDescription: New Clover Press hardcover art book collecting the amazing Marvel artwork of Mike Zeck plus Kickstarter exclusives!

owner.bio: Chuyên gia phát triển dự án bất động sản và nông nghiệp công nghệ cao.

content:
![Image](https://i.kickstarter.com/assets/053/447/266/1718939f29b8bee2afe0310f73bc870c_original.jpg?fit=scale-down&origin=ugc&q=92&v=1776892790&width=680&sig=uUP%2FebXjNNctUxd5W2jLPZlKCV6BdfuKggC%2B6xWhx%2BU%3D)
Clover Press and Marvel are collaborating for The Marvel Art Of… books, a series of high-end, boutique artbooks that showcase legendary Marvel Comics artists, featuring iconic images alongside rare and never-before-seen artwork. The tenth book in the stunning series will be THE MARVEL ART OF MIKE ZECK, a high-end coffee table book, along with portfolios and prints that celebrate the career of the renowned comic book artist.

Breaking out at Marvel in 1977 as the penciler for Shang-Chi, Master of Kung-Fu, Mike Zeck grew to fame illustrating the twelve-issue Marvel Super-Heroes Secret Wars in which he designed the new black costume for Spider-Man! Among his mile-long list of credits includes the landmark Spider-Man story, "Kraven’s Last Hunt," that brought a new, darker tone to the Spider-Man mythos. He is remembered the most for work on the first Punisher mini-series in 1986 that has influenced every artist who has since illustrated the character.

"I’m excited to see so much of my Marvel work brought together in one prestige-format volume featuring the characters, covers, stories, and artwork that have connected with readers over the years, and happy to be able to share it with the fans who have supported my work throughout my career." —Mike Zeck

The Marvel Art of Mike Zeck collects Zeck's most stunning, most action-packed, and most well-loved Marvel illustrations from Marvel titles like Captain America, Spider-Man, Punisher and more in a 224-page 9″ x 12″ high-end coffee table book. The campaign will also feature 11″ x 17″ prints, stickers, a puzzle, signed books and more. The Marvel Art Of… series debuted in 2023 with The Marvel Art of David Mack and The Marvel Art of Alex Maleev, followed by stunning books for Michael Allred, Russell Dauterman, Mike Del Mundo, Dan dos Santos, Tyler Kirkham, David Nakayama, and Michael Turner.

content:
![Image](https://i.kickstarter.com/assets/053/511/367/0f02f7e9ffc53caba663d255285c52cf_original.png?fit=scale-down&origin=ugc&q=100&v=1777362056&width=680&sig=0EY54Vn4nTO9iWUVToL8eHYUdjVCpPFpglY6bCN1bzQ%3D)
This deck started out as a question: What if feelings aren't problems to solve? 

Feelings live in the nonverbal, non-visual world. They are first experienced as embodied sensation: pressure, heat, tightness, numbness, etc. Because of this, I sometimes struggle to name them as they can feel outside of cohesive language. 

I began creating metaphors to capture their essence—giving them bodies. A tangible form I could look at and have it reflect back to me how I am feeling. Something I could recognize.

Over the last six years, I've illustrated 50 different emotions. Each one taking between 20-40 hours, received my singular attention. Art is such an intimate process and in spending so much time with these ideas, I started to feel like each was my companion. I began to wonder: What if I could see shame, fear, discomfort not just as experiences but as friends? The more I got to know them, the more it felt like their goal was to keep me safe. 

This practice has utterly changed me. While I’m often still slow to know what I’m feeling, spending active time the depth of these ideas has rearranged my internal world to be a much safer and experiential space. What if the gateway to loving myself is the radical acceptance of my emotions? 

This deck is the result: a hand-illustrated emotional ecosystem designed to help you witness your feelings, understand their purpose, and build a relationship with your inner world. It is not a tool for fixing yourself, but a practice for meeting yourself.

content:
The Threshold Tarot: Now It's A Full Deck
This is a Kickstarter to fund a print run of the full 78-card deck of the Threshold Tarot. It is a deck that has been half my life in the making from idea to result. The figures in it are real people that inhabit my internal world, and the symbolism has been worked out from the guiding principles of tarot as set out by Aleister Crowley in the Book of Thoth. The resultant deck is as fresh as a Spring morning. The symbolic language I've used is informed by a lifetime of personal magickal and devotional practice. The deck feels earthy, dirty, touched by the divine madness of Dionysus, and absolutely stuffed with queers.

The artwork is all hand-drawn, starting with wet ink on paper. There is nothing of my magick within AI generated anything: the gods demand blood and pigment. 

I thumbnailed onto brown recycled paper in crayon and paint marker, cut in lines with an ink pen I've used since childhood, and then dragged the resultant work over onto my big beautiful Wacom to clean it up. The people within the cards have their own lives and stories which informed how I positioned them, what cards they appear in. I go into this a little in the booklet, but honestly, I want you to develop your own relationship with the artwork I have made. Read the images closely, and let the little environments speak to you.

The first iteration of this deck, the major-arcana-only version, had no cleaning done to it at all: all the linework was exactly as it sat in my sketchbook. This version is much cleaner, crisper, and well-balanced. It has been an exquisite pleasure revisiting artwork I made 6 years ago to find that I both still loved it and could improve upon it. This whole project has been an utter delight to me, in all its frustrations, head-scratchings, hand-cramps, and "aha!"s.
